skill.hypothesis: Phenomenon: short-horizon reversal with medium-horizon drift in small-cap equities; Measurement object: persistent state formed by recent return displacement and its recovery/asymmetry relative to volatility and trading activity; Persistence hypothesis: sharp short-term moves accompanied by unstable path features tend to mean-revert, while smoother medium-horizon accumulation persists weakly.
skill.grammar: Combine (i) short-horizon displacement level with negative sign, (ii) recovery/reversal proxy via delayed and differenced multi-day returns, and (iii) path-instability penalties from range/open-close/overnight and recent volatility; optionally retain a weak medium-horizon state term and a light liquidity interaction to separate transient shocks from persistent trends.
skill.applicability: More predictable in retail-dominated, high-turnover small-cap regimes with noisy short-term overreaction and limited trend durability; weaker in strongly policy-driven momentum bursts.
successes: Negative loading on recent 1-5 day return levels combined with negative loading on delay/delta of 5-day return to capture reversal after abrupt displacement.
Use of path/asymmetry controls (range1, open_close, overnight, max/min recent daily return) to distinguish unstable jumps from smoother persistent moves.
Keep medium-horizon state sparse and weakly positive (ret20/ret60, rank_ret20) rather than extending windows mechanically.
failures: Can fail during broad speculative momentum phases where short-term continuation dominates reversal.
Can fail after structural regime shifts or policy shocks when overnight gaps encode genuine information rather than transitory imbalance.
May underperform in very illiquid names where measured reversal proxies are dominated by trading frictions instead of mispricing.

skill.applicability: More predictable in CSI1000-like small-cap, retail-heavy, high-turnover regimes where short-term price pressure and noisy jumps are common; weaker during coordinated speculative momentum or policy-led continuation bursts.
